title: Mixed CPU workloads
purpose: Measure per-core and aggregate CPU performance across hashing, compression, serialisation, integer and floating-point work representative of web server duty.
preparation: Generate five deterministic corpora from CORPUS_SEED via SplitMix64.
calibration: Per workload and shape, grow a probe from one iteration by a bounded proportional step until a repetition exceeds a quarter of target_rep_ms, then extrapolate linearly. Capped at 2^24 iterations.
warmup: warmup_reps repetitions per metric, streamed and retained but excluded from statistics.

workloads.description: SHA-256 over a 1 MiB deterministic buffer.
DEFLATE level 6 over a 512 KiB English-like corpus.
Serialise and parse a 64-record product document.

workloads.represents: ORDER BY, index maintenance, log processing

workloads.description: 128x128 dense f64 matrix multiply, i-k-j ordered.

derived_metrics.note: Below 0.5 on a dedicated-vCPU plan suggests SMT saturation, thermal limits or oversubscription.

validation: Every workload must produce at least 5 measured repetitions.
Repetitions shorter than 20 ms are rejected as timer-noise dominated.
Coefficient of variation above 0.15 raises a high-variance warning and downgrades the result to Degraded.
cleanup: None required: the module allocates only heap memory, released when it returns.
limitations: Measures the CPU as the operating system presents it. Inside a container or a cgroup-limited VM the result describes that sandbox, not the host.
Does not use hand-written SIMD; it measures what a normal optimised program achieves, including whatever the compiler auto-vectorises.
Multi-threaded shapes measure throughput, not parallel speed-up of a single problem, so they do not capture inter-core latency or lock contention.

scoring.note: Reference anchors are declared targets, not measurements. See docs/SCORING-SYSTEM.md.
